title: The Thin Channel Where Voices Learn to Speak Again

features.name: water-that-carries-breath
features.desc-on-touch: The channel runs with runoff so thin it's barely wetting. But in it you hear murmurs—not words yet, but the shape of words remembering how to form.

features.name: the-voices-that-learned-to-whisper
features.desc-on-touch: Coming back one by one. Each separate now. Not unified song but a conversation with gaps in it. The gaps are where the real listening happens.

features.name: stone-that-remembers-echo
features.desc-on-touch: The narrow channel carved by silence learning it's not permanent. The walls remember what was not said. Now they begin to speak it back.

features.name: the-interval-where-speech-learns-shape
features.desc-on-touch: A gap between utterances that has become space. Not a silence anymore—something more like breathing. The void has learned to become rhythm.

features.name: mosses-that-learned-a-song
features.desc-on-touch: Growing along the channel-edge. Their green is humming very quietly. They heard the silence first, and now they're hearing it end.

inscription: from the shallows where words learned silence comes the thin sound of words learning to speak again without forgetting what they learned

file.note: Field recording of water and small utterances. Status: germinating. The voices are still learning who they are in the channel.

reverie.title: REVERIE — the creek at first light where she taught you to l
narr: You both stood in the thin water, barely ankle-deep.
She said: listen wrong. Listen for the gaps.
You stood there long enough that birds came back.
Long enough that the water learned your names.
She smiled at the moment the silence turned over—
the instant it became breath instead of absence.
